newsitem.title: GERMANY: German minister warns against isolating Algeria.
newsitem.headline: German minister warns against isolating Algeria.

text.p: A German minister said on Wednesday the increasing isolation of Algeria would only worsen conditions for its people and vowed to work to improve economic ties between the two countries.

Werner Hoyer, state secretary in the foreign ministry, told a news conference in Bonn after a three-day trip to Algeria that the importance of the violence-ridden North African nation should not be undervalued.

"It is my feeling that we would be making a mistake if we allow this country to slip away into isolation," Hoyer said. "The perspectives for the people will become darker and darker if there is no longer any contact abroad."
An estimated 50,000 people have been killed in violence which erupted after the authorities in January 1992 cancelled a general election in which Islamists had taken a strong lead.
Hoyer led a delegation of about 20 German industrial leaders on the trip to Algeria. They met political leaders, opposition figures, journalists and industrialists in Algeria.

He said that he felt his trip had raised some hopes for people in Algeria, although he admitted that he felt somewhat uncomfortable about being in the country where Moslem fundamentalists had also targeted many foreigners.

Bilateral trade between Algeria and Germany has fallen to about two billion marks ($1.30 billion) in recent years and Hoyer said many factories in Algeria, which were equipped with German machinery in past decades, were badly in need of replacement parts.

"Algeria is a highly interesting (trade) partner with potential for the future," Hoyer said. "Algeria is a veritable museum of German industry. Many of the machines and plants are screaming out for spare parts and repairs."
German exports which once totalled between two and three billion marks a year have now fallen to about 800 million marks. ($1=1.5405 Mark)
